newsitem.title: INDIA: Profit-taking clips Bombay shares rally, end lower.
newsitem.headline: Profit-taking clips Bombay shares rally, end lower.

text.p: ** (1015 GMT) Bombay shares shed sharp early gains to end
lower as profit-takers halt five-day winning streak ** Traders say decline anticipated after index soared
seven percent this week ** Benchmark Bombay share index closes 8.78 points lower at
a provisional 4,325.12 -- after peaking at 4,393.29 ** Activity mainly in index-linked stocks which is favoured
by foreign funds ** National exchange index ends 6.55 points lower at a
Bombay share prices finished lower on Thursday as profit-taking snapped a five-day rally and traders said they expected more unwinding of positions.
"This reaction was well anticipated," said Sunil Kothari at brokerage Nagindas S. Kothari. "A correction was due because the market had gone up too sharply."
Local players were encouraged to cut exposures because Friday is the last day of the weekly account, he said.
"I expect more selling tomorrow," he said. "But, it could rebound if foreign funds come in aggressively."
Hopes of an economic upturn propelled by falling interest rates and easy money conditions are luring foreign funds into Indian equities, an international fund manager told Reuters.

"I think it's a good chance that you will see the economy starting to pick up in the second half. Some early signs are there, but nothing concrete," Nikhil Khattau, chief executive at SUN F&C Asset Management (I) Pvt Ltd.
The markets are discounting the long-term gains. "I think we'll have to be slightly ahead of the herd," he said.
Analysts said foreign funds buying was restricted to blue-chip shares with the demand not spilling to the broader section.
"We're seeing buying from U.S. based index-funds," said fund manager S.M. Athalye, associate vice president (investments) at Tata Asset Management Ltd.
"The buying is only in index stocks," he said.
Software stock Infosys finished 20 rupees higher at 1,960, off 1,905.25 day's low, after the firm said its board will finalise first quarter financial results on July 7.
